alternatives: Prospective audit of new airway events from now on (refused: cannot show change since 2023 and takes years to accrue events)
Simple before-after comparison of two periods (refused: ignores the pre-existing trend and co-interventions)
Survey of anaesthetists about alerts (refused as the main design: measures opinion, not recognition)
whyNotMoreComplex: A controlled design across hospitals is not possible because other hospitals' records are not accessible; a segmented series within the hospital is the strongest feasible design.
rationale: The alert system started on a known date and the hospital holds records on both sides of it, so a retrospective segmented comparison of recognition before airway management is the simplest design that answers the committee's question. A before-after rise elsewhere (claim c1), the gap between display and reading (claim c2) and the rate of unanticipated difficulty (claim c3) set the planning values.

decision.statement: Conduct a retrospective segmented time series of documented recognition of known airway difficulty before later airway management, January 2019 to August 2026, from the difficult airway database and anaesthetic records, reporting co-interventions and database capture.
decision.question: How should the hospital evaluate its difficult airway alert system?

criteria.text: Recognition can change after alert systems but display is not recognition, so a local measure of recognition would inform the committee.
Too few later airway management episodes exist on either side of the change for a time series.

gates.requirement: Approval to access the difficult airway database and linked anaesthetic records
gates.evidence: Caldicott guardian approval CG-2026-118 dated 2 September 2026, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Research governance classification of the study
gates.evidence: Trust research office classification RSE-26-044 dated 9 September 2026, supplied by the investigator

decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c3 from retrieved records; both gates met on investigator-supplied approvals.

summary: Retrospective segmented series recommended; the decision rests on three ledger claims and both gates are met.
